_comment: Verifier verdict vectors. Written by scripts/verdict-vectors.py from docs/format-spec.md (§4, §5.5, §9.4, §9.8) and never by an implementation under test. Each case is a valid chain with one stated defect; `why` cites the rule. chain_cases: verify the entries (linking the first from previous_hash, empty for a whole chain) and compare verdict, the index and type of the FIRST break (-1 and "" when intact), tombstones_found and last_tombstone. entries_text_cases: text is the content of an entries file; "entries" means it decodes, "not_entries" that it is refused as not being entries (an error, never a broken chain). anchor_text_cases: text is an anchor's JSON; "parses" or "refused". bind_cases: a keyless bind of anchor to entries with previous_anchor_hash; expected.error true means the anchor is refused as malformed; otherwise compare outcome, bound, tombstones and entries_not_bound. No case needs a key.

chain_cases.name: intact
chain_cases.why: four well-formed v3 entries

chain_cases.name: starts_at_global_seq_1
chain_cases.why: §5.5: the first global_seq is not fixed; the hosted platform starts at 1

chain_cases.name: starts_at_global_seq_1001
chain_cases.why: §5.5: nor is a later start a break

chain_cases.name: content_edited
chain_cases.why: an edited content hash no longer hashes to the stored chain hash

chain_cases.name: sequence_gap
chain_cases.why: global_seq must rise by one

chain_cases.name: timestamp_in_another_offset
chain_cases.why: §4: a stored timestamp in any spelling but YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ is a break, even though it names the instant that was hashed

chain_cases.name: timestamp_with_no_fraction
chain_cases.why: §4: a stored timestamp in any spelling but YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ is a break, even though it names the instant that was hashed

chain_cases.name: timestamp_with_nanoseconds
chain_cases.why: §4: a stored timestamp in any spelling but YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ is a break, even though it names the instant that was hashed

chain_cases.name: timestamp_lowercase_z
chain_cases.why: §4: a stored timestamp in any spelling but YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ is a break, even though it names the instant that was hashed

chain_cases.name: content_hash_not_a_digest
chain_cases.why: §5.5: re-linked, so the hashes agree; the shape does not

chain_cases.name: content_hash_uppercase
chain_cases.why: §5.5: lowercase hex

chain_cases.name: content_hash_64_hex
chain_cases.why: §2: a content hash is SHA-512, 128 hex characters

chain_cases.name: chain_hash_not_a_digest
chain_cases.why: §5.5: on any entry

chain_cases.name: unknown_format_version
chain_cases.why: §2.2: never guessed

chain_cases.name: v3_entry_carrying_run_id
chain_cases.why: §2.2: v3 binds neither run_id nor sequence_num

chain_cases.name: tombstone
chain_cases.why: §5.1: an erased entry is not a break; its stored chain hash is carried forward

chain_cases.name: tombstone_content_hash_on_an_ordinary_entry
chain_cases.why: §5.5: the content hash alone does not make a tombstone; the entry is recomputed and does not match

chain_cases.name: tombstone_with_a_malformed_chain_hash
chain_cases.why: §5.5: chain_hash is a digest on every entry, tombstones included

chain_cases.name: tombstone_with_an_unknown_format
chain_cases.why: §5.5: what a tombstone declares is still checked

chain_cases.name: entries_before_a_tombstone_rewritten
chain_cases.why: §5.5, THE LIMITATION: this chain was tampered with and verifies. A verifier cannot detect it and MUST report last_tombstone so the caller knows entries 0 to 2 are not verified

chain_cases.name: tombstone_with_another_timestamp_spelling
chain_cases.why: §5.5: the only checks on a tombstone are its chain hash shape, its content hash format, its declared format and global_seq

chain_cases.name: timestamp_that_is_not_a_real_instant
chain_cases.why: §4: the right shape, and no such day

chain_cases.name: two_defects_timestamp_before_field_shape
chain_cases.why: §5.5: the timestamp is judged before the other field shapes

chain_cases.name: two_defects_chain_hash_shape_first
chain_cases.why: §5.5: chain_hash is checked first on every entry

chain_cases.name: two_defects_unknown_format_before_field_shape
chain_cases.why: §5.5: an entry of an unknown format has no field shapes to judge

chain_cases.name: segment_with_its_predecessor_hash
chain_cases.why: a segment links from the hash supplied

chain_cases.name: segment_without_its_predecessor_hash
chain_cases.why: and from nothing, it does not

chain_cases.name: malformed_previous_hash
chain_cases.why: §5.5: the supplied predecessor hash is a digest

bind_cases.name: chain_broken
bind_cases.why: the chain does not verify, so nothing is bound

bind_cases.name: truncated_from_the_front_and_relinked
bind_cases.why: the remainder verifies on its own; the anchor's committed first entry is gone

bind_cases.name: height_mismatch
bind_cases.why: entry_count is not the chain's length

bind_cases.name: wrong_predecessor_hash
bind_cases.why: §9.4: the predecessor's hash is inside the anchor's own

bind_cases.name: first_anchor_naming_a_predecessor
bind_cases.why: §9.8: the seed hash goes with the seed id only

bind_cases.name: chain_grown_since_the_anchor
bind_cases.why: §9.7: a bind is over exactly the entries given. The caller passes the prefix the anchor covers; given the grown chain, the anchor's last entry is not the last entry

bind_cases.name: chain_broken_after_a_tombstone
bind_cases.why: the counts are what the walk saw, whatever the outcome

bind_cases.name: predecessor_checked_before_the_head
bind_cases.why: §9.8: two defects, a first anchor naming a predecessor and a wrong head; the predecessor is reported

bind_cases.name: verified_through_above_entry_count
bind_cases.why: §9.8: refused as a malformed anchor, not reported as an outcome

bind_cases.name: bound_over_a_tombstone
bind_cases.why: §5.5: a lawful erasure does not break the anchor, and the result reports that entries 0 to 2 are not bound

bind_cases.name: entries_before_a_tombstone_rewritten
bind_cases.why: §5.5, THE LIMITATION: tampered, and it binds. entries_not_bound is what tells the caller

bind_cases.name: last_entry_given_a_tombstone_content_hash
bind_cases.why: §5.5: one tombstone rule in every path. The last entry keeps its chain hash and takes a TOMBSTONE: content hash, with every other entry replaced; it is not a tombstone, and the chain is broken
